create.name: Robert Rosenbaum
create.bio:
Robert Rosenbaum, known as Bob and by the dharma name Meikyo, teaches Zen meditation and Dayan (Wild Goose) qigong in Sacramento. He has practised meditation and movement for more than fifty years. Sojun Mel Weitsman gave him lay entrustment in the Soto school, Karen Terzano authorised him (denkai) in the Ordinary Mind Zen line, and was asked by Master Hui Liu to carry forward her lineage of Wild Goose qigong. Before turning to teaching full time he had a long career as a psychologist, and he once taught in India as a Fulbright scholar.

At Meadowmind, the small centre he started, he serves as guiding teacher of Ordinary Mind Zen Sacramento, a lay sangha that keeps Soto-style forms but runs without hierarchy and welcomes meditators of any background to its weekly sittings. Alongside zazen the group practises the long flowing Dayan sequence of sixty-four movements, combined with natural breathing and Taoist sitting meditation. His recorded talks, given at Houston Zen Center, Berkeley Zen Center and the Commonwealth Club, touch on emptiness and compassion, working with feelings, and the meeting of Zen with the Tao Te Ching, and he has written books on Zen and Taoist teachings.

courses.title: Ordinary Mind Zen Sacramento: Weekly Zazen
courses.description: Weekly sittings at Meadowmind in Sacramento on Monday mornings and Wednesday evenings, in Soto-style forms within a lay sangha. Newcomers contact the group before attending; a year-long precepts study is also offered.

courses.title: Dayan (Wild Goose) Qigong Practice
courses.description: Group practice of the Dayan qigong form, with its long flowing sequences, self-massage and Taoist meditation. Sessions are for people with some qigong background; class information is on the site's resources page.

free_resources.title: Compassion and Emptiness
free_resources.description: A recorded dharma talk from Houston Zen Center (2014) on how compassion and emptiness fit together.

free_resources.title: Practicing with Feelings
free_resources.description: A 2018 talk at Houston Zen Center on bringing emotions into Zen practice rather than pushing them away.

free_resources.title: Zen and the Tao Te Ching
free_resources.description: A 2013 talk at the Commonwealth Club on reading the Tao Te Ching through Zen practice.

free_resources.title: Mind Is Ungraspable
free_resources.description: A 2005 talk from Berkeley Zen Center on the Zen teaching that mind cannot be grasped.
